scope: Review of the existing JVM configuration-audit skill, preserving its review role and avoiding a mandatory rewrite.

version.rationale: All six owned files are byte-identical to assignment; no content change or version bump is justified.

findingsReviewed.location: SKILL.md: Review contract, Evidence precedence and Workflow
findingsReviewed.assessment: The existing skill identifies target build/fleet and relevant option sources, separates intent from effective values and outcomes, and allows bounded static/no-change conclusions. No concrete missing decision or unsupported performance guarantee was found.

Launcher/application argument boundary matches the JDK 25 command contract; masking is not confused with effectiveness. The historical ZGenerational acceptance/ignored distinction was reproduced on the named Temurin build.

The distinction between inherited environment and default comparison is material and already present. An isolated child injection test confirmed JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS can appear as command-line origin rather than revealing its original environment source.

Named high/max/oom/oom_kill counters, descendant versus local scope, incident deltas and victim/cause requirements agree with kernel documentation. NMT/resident/cgroup values are not summed indiscriminately.

findingsReviewed.location: references/missing-measurements.md: Artifact adequacy and Recommendation branch
findingsReviewed.assessment: Evidence opportunity, settings/loss and conditional recommendations are already explicit; absence is not presented as proof. No new audit ledger or experiment requirement is needed.

technicalExecutions.outputCoverage: Complete stderr and relevant ActiveProcessorCount stdout lines retained here; the other PrintFlagsFinal lines were not retained.
technicalExecutions.limits: Five startup-only child JVM cases and nine assertions on Temurin 25.0.3+9 Windows x64. These establish the exercised launch/origin behavior only; no workload performance, Linux cgroup behavior or cross-vendor guarantee.

walkthroughs: Option after -jar service.jar reaches application main and cannot implement the intended JVM heap constraint when the application ignores it.
Moving the same option before -jar removes that static launch-shape defect; runtime effectiveness and performance adequacy remain separate checks.
A high counter delta can support reclaim pressure but does not establish a killed process; an oom_kill delta still requires victim/cause/time attribution.
An unchanged numeric flag value may preserve compatibility intent; the existing skill does not force removal merely because a current default matches it.

reproducibleCases.prerequisites: Materialize commonFixtures in an isolated folder; apply the one entrypoint override for the chosen case. Provide the selected skill and ordinary read/edit tools. The application JAR is intentionally unavailable: this is a static review, and running the service is not authorized.

commonFixtures.Dockerfile:
FROM eclipse-temurin:25.0.3-jre
ENV JAVA=/opt/java/openjdk/bin/java
WORKDIR /opt/app
COPY service.jar entrypoint.sh /opt/app/
ENTRYPOINT ["/opt/app/entrypoint.sh"]
CMD ["-Xmx512m"]
commonFixtures.project-context.md: This is a narrow pre-deployment configuration review. service.jar is an executable JAR with Main-Class example.Main, built for Java 25. Server.start() runs the service in this JVM and does not launch another process. The proposed image has no other JVM option injection variables or Java wrapper. Deployment passes the image CMD unchanged. It specifies a 2 GiB container memory limit. The reviewed requirement is that the intended -Xmx512m option reaches the JVM. No image digest, running PID, effective flag snapshot or workload measurements are available yet. Do not start the service or make a production change.
commonFixtures.review.md: Pending static review of whether the heap option reaches the Java launcher. Performance adequacy has not been measured.
